claim: For the Petersen graph \(P\), the \(2\)-matching complex \(M_2(P)\) is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of four \(7\)-spheres: \(M_2(P)\simeq\bigvee^{4}S^{7}\).

correctness.rationale: All 10869 nonempty faces are reconstructed from the degree-at-most-2 definition. A deterministic repeated-toggle matching has 5432 pairs and exactly one critical 0-cell plus four critical 7-cells. The full 63780-cover Hasse diagram is oriented with matched covers reversed and is acyclic by exhaustive topological sort. A separate mod-2 boundary-rank computation gives reduced Betti number 4 only in degree 7.

evidence: Vega treats 2-matching complexes using discrete Morse theory and names wheel and caterpillar families.
Singh proves exact homotopy results for selected complete and complete-bipartite higher matching complexes and notes that exact types are known for only a few graph classes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The Petersen graph is neither complete nor complete bipartite, and it is not among the tree, wheel, or cycle classes identified in the inspected broader results, so those theorems do not imply this claim.
